children: Copper hit a record high on Tuesday, as global supply tightened with the metal continuing to flow into the U.S. ahead of possible tariffs.
Three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange
was up 0.51% at $14,584 a metric ton as of 0700 GMT. Earlier in the session, it hit a record high of $14,617, surpassing the previous record set on Monday.
The most-traded copper contract on the Shanghai Futures Exchange
closed 1.29% higher at 110,620 yuan ($16,483.88) a ton, after rising as much as 1.54% to 110,890 yuan, its highest since January 30.
In the U.S., COMEX inventories (HG-STX-COMEX) swelled to a record 766,795 short tons, or 695,624 metric tons, as of last week.

“The still-elevated COMEX-LME price spread suggests physical copper continues to flow into the United States, deepening the supply tightness in markets outside the U.S.,” an analyst at Chinese broker Everbright Futures said.
Copper stocks in LME-registered warehouses saw more than 51% of their warrants cancelled.
Inventories monitored by the SHFE (CU-SGH-STX) stood at around 63,000 tons last week, down 85% from a mid-March peak and the lowest since January 2024.
A premium of LME cash copper over the three-month contract (CMCU0-3), known as a backwardation, persisted, signalling tight near-term availability of the metal.

Elsewhere, the U.S. dollar hovered around recent lows, making metals denominated in the greenback cheaper for holders of other currencies, although expectations that the Federal Reserve could raise interest rates in September remained a headwind for risk assets.
Zinc also rallied, with three-month LME zinc
up 0.54% at $4,005 a ton as of 0700 GMT, after touching $4,035, its highest in more than four years.
The most-traded SHFE zinc contract
rose 1.89% to close the day at 27,505 yuan a ton.
Among other LME metals, aluminium
was flat, lead
rose 0.13%, nickel
was flat and tin
fell 0.18%.
On the SHFE, aluminium
rose 0.47%, lead
fell 0.25%, nickel
slipped 0.38% and tin
gained 0.48%.
($1 = 6.7108 Chinese yuan renminbi)
